3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: With a final whistle, the Maroon Train came to a stop in the middle of the Forest of October.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: I opened the window to look outside. The air was cool and I enjoyed the smell of nature for a brief moment.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I straightened my jacket as she approached.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: With a haughty sniff, she turned around and left the wagon.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: A few minutes later, another train pulled in behind ours and stopped with a whistle.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: She looked much older and more tired than the last time I had seen her. Clearly, the war had taken its toll on her.

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “What's wrong with being out in nature?"

15.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
15.text: “You couldn't have chosen a better location, could you?"

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “You are here to sign your capitulation. You will meet me wherever I please.”

17.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
17.text: “Don't take me for a fool, Mr. Rayne.”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “Shut up. I don't want to spend any more time than I need with you.”

19.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
19.text: “Hah. Such vulgarity. Barbarians, all of you.”

20.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
20.text: “As if your victory was not enough, you felt compelled to drag me out to the middle of a forest to cement it."

21.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
21.text: “And not just any forest, of course.”

22.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
22.text: “This is the same place where the ceasefire was signed for the 15-Day War.”

23.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
23.text: “You really are trying to humiliate me, aren't you?”

24.speaker: Player
24.text: “Of course not. This is a simple coincidence. That's all.”

25.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
25.text: “Give me the bloody papers. I can't stand breathing the same air as you.”

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “Ms. Livingston, you are forgetting the protocol. I expect you to say please first.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “You are not being a good loser, Ms. Livingston.”

28.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
28.text: “You're not only a barbarian, you're a liar."

29.speaker: Player
29.text: “Yes, I am. So what? What can you do without your country, Queen of Rumburg?”

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: She struggled to come up with a response, then gave up and sighed heavily.

35.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
35.text: “Please... hand me the papers, Mr. Rayne.”

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: Beatrice angrily scribbled her signature and put down the pen before passing on the document. I signed the agreement and gave it to my assistant.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: The witnesses were called for the signing of the agreement titled the 'Treaty of Rayne'.

38.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
38.text: “There you go. Are you quite satisfied?”

40.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
40.text: “I'm sure you would act the same way if you were in my place."

41.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
41.text: “I hereby proclaim that you can go fuck yourself."

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “I don't want to see your face again.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Before you go, there is one more thing.”

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “Don't ever forget who your Suzerain is.”

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: She paused for a second and glared at me in pure fury.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: My cabin rocked gently as the Maroon Train sped through the leafy outskirts of Estord.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: An assistant knocked sharply, then slid the door open. He approached my desk and handed me the day's newspaper and a letter.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: The first thing I saw was the headline: 'Conqueror Rayne' written in giant letters.

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: 'I wanted to congratulate you on our victory against Rumburg. We showed them who they were messing with.'

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: "Is that how you old folks say it? I know I could have called, but a letter felt more appropriate for the occasion."

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: "But there's nothing I can do to change any of that now."

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: 'All I can ask is this: When you see the Queen, give her a big fat middle finger from me."

101.speaker: Narrator
101.text: 'P.S.: Mom is fine and Deana might have a boyfriend.'

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: "I can't help but think about all my friends and squadmates on the front lines. I know I'm lucky to be deployed here in Holsord, but part of me wishes I could've fought with them."

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: "Still... I wonder if you and the other bigwigs back in Holsord know the real cost of this war. It's not just that I could've died. It's that some of the things I did make me wish I had."
